inconsistencies: Logging configuration is contested by three overlapping PRs: #34038 (replace -loglevel with -trace, RPC trace controls), #35387 (standalone -loglevel plus a new loglevel RPC) and #35355 (which does the -trace rename AND the atomic bitmask work). Review #34038 first and settle the interface; #35387 is an explicit competing alternative and #35355 should be split or rebased on the outcome.

#35322 and #35355 implement the same internal change (replacing the Logger category level map/mutex with atomic category bitmasks). One of them is redundant; #35322 is the narrower, non-draft version and should be reviewed first.

Settings chain, order matters: #36295 (removes wrapper overloads) -> #31260 (typed Setting registration) -> #16545 (ALLOW_BOOL/INT/STRING enforcement) -> #17580 (ALLOW_LIST) -> #17783 and #17493 -> #17581. #17783 and #17493 both sit on #16545+#17580 and cannot be reviewed meaningfully before them, despite #17783 scoring near the top on its own.
util::Result chain: #25665 is the base; #26022 (ResultPtr) sits on it; #25722 needs both; #29700 needs #25665. Reviewing #25665 resolves the design questions for all three.
Logging macro chain: #34778 blocks #29256, which in turn is the stated prerequisite for kernel logging #30342 and wallet logging #30343. #34778 was a band below the work it unblocks; raised to P2.

#36537 and #36550 (both fametrano) address the same problem, residual key material in hash object state; #36550 also supersedes #36551. Review them as one unit, #36537 first since it covers HMAC and MuSig2.
#36442 -> #36443: the multipath reconstruction PR is meaningless until the single-object representation lands.
#36105 -> #36190: #36190 is purely tests for the Windows wrapper behaviour introduced by #36105 and must not be merged ahead of it.

#19460 depends on #10102 and #29409 and unblocks #19461; its utils-relevant content is only init/option scaffolding, so it stays marginal in this category regardless of the multiprocess project's importance.
result.notes: The per-PR assessments produced no P1 at all for a 63-PR category whose stated first concern is correctness and safety of primitives. Three fixes clearly meet the bar and were promoted: block-data destruction during reindex (#35524), an uncatchable abort on disk-write failure (#36049), and out-of-bounds reads in the UniValue tokenizer (#35281). Everything else keeps its band except #34778, raised to match the work it blocks. Several PRs here (silent payments #32966, compact-block prefill #35558, parallel index sync #26966) are large pieces of work whose home is another category; they are ranked only on the shared primitive or utility they add.
